text:
1. The twenty-second chapter of Genesis raises a question that is never answered.
2. In Genesis 22, Abraham is commanded to take his son.
3. The son is described as Abraham's only son.
4. The son is described as one whom Abraham loves.
5. The narrator of Genesis 22 tells us nothing of what Abraham feels.
6. The narrator never looks into Abraham's inner life.
7. Abraham does not protest the command.
8. Abraham does not bargain over the command.
9. Abraham pleaded for Sodom on an earlier occasion.
10. The Abraham of Genesis 22 shows none of the traits of the man who pleaded for Sodom.
11. In Genesis 22, Abraham appears less as a character than as a silence.
12. The whole chapter turns on Abraham's silence.
